review_notes: I read the whole target file and searched the ErdosGinzburgZiv sources for similar proofs. The same five-step calc chain (rewrite the sum with `val_eq` or `coord_eq`, convert to `Finset.affineCombination`, apply `map_affineCombination`, convert back, then `Fintype.sum_congr`) appears in three proofs. They are `ConvexCombination.coord_eq` in ConvexFlag/Basic.lean (lines 209-230), `ConvexCombination.eval_eq` in ConvexFlag/WeakHull.lean (lines 93-111), and `ConvexCombination.map_on_polytope` in the target (lines 84-102). I also saw a repeated "some weight is positive" block (the `by_contra!` argument) in Restrict.lean, Reduction.lean and the target. It is short, so I did not report it. I did not report the duplicated `Point.map` and `SubdivisionMap.point` definitions, because the rubric concerns repeated proof machinery. I could not compile anything. The proposed lemma and the rewrites are sketches that I did not check against Lean, and I invented no Mathlib lemma names. The only Mathlib lemmas relied on are `Finset.map_affineCombination` and `Finset.affineCombination_eq_linear_combination`, both of which the existing proofs already use.

findings.problem: The final calc of `map_on_polytope` redoes a general fact: an affine map commutes with a finite sum weighted by coefficients that sum to 1. It does this by hand. The chain is `sum → Finset.affineCombination (affineCombination_eq_linear_combination) → map_affineCombination → back to sum (affineCombination_eq_linear_combination + rfl)`. The same chain appears in `ConvexCombination.coord_eq` (ConvexFlag/Basic.lean) with `(F.transition hy).real` as the map, and in `ConvexCombination.eval_eq` (ConvexFlag/WeakHull.lean) with `xi.toAffine` as the map. The three copies share the active-index subtype `A`, the proof `hs : ∑ weight = 1`, the two `by simpa using hs` side conditions, and the `rfl` finishing step. Only the affine map and the final `Fintype.sum_congr` step differ. Any change to the active-subtype or weight handling has to be made in three places.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma in ConvexFlag/Basic.lean before `ConvexCombination.coord_eq`, so all three files see it. It would read roughly: `theorem EGZ.ConvexFlag.affineMap_sum_smul_of_sum_eq_one {A : Type*} [Fintype A] {V W : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [AddTorsor V V] ... (T : V →ᵃ[ℝ] W) (z : A → V) (w : A → ℝ) (hs : ∑ i, w i = 1) : T (∑ i, w i • z i) = ∑ i, w i • T (z i)`. Here `V` and `W` stand for the `RealCoord` spaces, which are real vector spaces. The proof is the existing chain: `classical`, rewrite both sums with `Finset.affineCombination_eq_linear_combination _ _ _ hs`, apply `Finset.map_affineCombination` for `Finset.univ`, and close with `rfl` for the composed function. The three users then shrink. In `map_on_polytope`, the calc becomes `change fibre result.base result.val = _; rw [c.val_eq, affineMap_sum_smul_of_sum_eq_one (fibre result.base) z (fun i ↦ weight i) hs]; exact Fintype.sum_congr _ _ fun i ↦ congrArg (weight i • ·) (hcomm (c.base_isLUB.1 i i.2) (points i).val (points i).val_mem)`. In `coord_eq`, the first four calc steps become `rw [show result.coord hy = _ from rfl, c.val_eq, affineMap_sum_smul_of_sum_eq_one (F.transition hy).real z _ hs]`, followed by its existing `Fintype.sum_congr` step. In `eval_eq`, the same lemma is applied with `xi.toAffine` and `c.coord_eq hxi`, followed by its existing congruence step.
findings.benefit: The proof of this fact (affine maps preserve sums whose weights total 1) is stated once instead of three times, and `map_on_polytope` shrinks from about 19 calc lines to a rewrite plus the one genuinely specific step, which is the commutation `hcomm`. A reader can see that the only new content is `hcomm` and the base-compatibility. A future change to the active-subtype handling needs one edit rather than three.
